title: A dynamical positive Cartan metric selects a frame or runs to the noncompact boundary

claim.statement: Promoting the positive Cartan metric to an auxiliary field does not generically restore Lorentz symmetry after elimination: its noncompact orbit has no finite invariant average, timelike couplings select a frame, and null couplings can run to infinite rapidity.
claim.scope: Explicit SO(1,1) subgroup diagnostic inside SO(2,3).

interpretation: The symmetric space of Cartan metrics is noncompact, so group averaging is not a normalizable symmetry-restoration mechanism.
A matter/compensator configuration can pin the auxiliary metric, but the resulting vacuum still carries a preferred Cartan frame.
Null configurations expose boundary runaways unless an additional stabilizing potential is added; such a potential itself selects structure.
falsifiers: A fully gauge-redundant formulation with no Cartan-metric observables could evade the preferred-frame conclusion.
A compact quotient or contour prescription might regularize an average but would add nontrivial global input.
The SO(1,1) subtoy is a necessary diagnostic, not a full path-integral theorem for SO(2,3).
nextBranches: Treat the Cartan metric as gauge fixing rather than a physical field and identify BRST-invariant observables.
Explore single-compensator constrained formulations that avoid a positive metric entirely.
Test whether the programme's pseudo-unitary carrier metric can provide bounded response terms without selecting a spacetime Cartan frame.
